requirements.evidence: All contract items present: .env.example APP_NAME=PegaFila/APP_LOCALE=pt_BR; phpunit.xml pins APP_NAME, APP_LOCALE, APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE; config/mail.php 'markdown' => ['theme' => 'pegafila', ...]; pegafila.css uses #0f7490 on .button-primary (present in every action mail); lang/pt_BR.json adds "Reset your password" and "Verify your email address"; routes/web.php defines password.request/email (throttle:6,1)/reset/update under 'guest' and verification.verify with ['auth','signed','throttle:6,1']; PasswordResetLinkController::store always returns back()->with('status', __('passwords.sent')); NewPasswordController::store validates token/email/password (min 8, letters, mixedCase, numbers, confirmed), rotates remember_token, fires PasswordReset, redirects to '/'; VerifyEmailController uses EmailVerificationRequest (403 on id/hash mismatch) and redirects to '/'. Reset form has a single email input.

conventions.evidence: Tests shipped for every endpoint; CHANGELOG.md updated under [Unreleased] and new docs/ops/account-mail.md; PHPDoc on public controller methods. Deviation: NewPasswordController::store validates three fields inline ($request->validate([... 'token', 'email', 'password' ...])) where conventions call for a Form Request beyond one or two fields. Views duplicate the full <head> boilerplate rather than sharing markup, though layouts are out of scope for this task.

security.evidence: No enumeration: identical status on unknown address (PasswordResetLinkController::store ignores the broker result); throttle:6,1 on password.email; verification route is auth+signed+throttled and EmailVerificationRequest checks id/hash; strong password rule; remember_token rotated; all view output uses {{ }} escaping; forceFill limited to password/remember_token. Only nit: unpinned CDN Bulma fallback without SRI in auth views.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/AccountMailTest.php checks config pins, theme color, rendered pt-BR subject/greeting/button/body/subcopy and absence of 'having trouble clicking'; PasswordResetTest.php covers form render, existing vs unknown email (no enumeration), validation, throttling (429), guest-only, single email input, valid/invalid token, weak password dataset, missing token/email; EmailVerificationTest.php covers signed URL, success + Verified event, wrong hash, other user's id, unsigned link. Small gap: guest-only test does not hit password.reset/password.update.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses Laravel's Password broker, ResetPassword/VerifyEmail notifications and EmailVerificationRequest; controllers are minimal. pegafila.css is a 299-line copy of the default theme, which is needed because a custom theme replaces default.css. The two auth views duplicate head/Vite/CDN boilerplate.

readability.evidence: Clear controller names and focused methods with explanatory docblocks (e.g. 'The response is identical either way so the form never reveals whether an address is registered'). Nit: stray double blank line in resources/views/auth/reset-password.blade.php:19-20; inline style="max-width: 28rem;" in both views.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task. app/Models/User.php now implements MustVerifyEmail, which is not required for the notification/route and changes behaviour for future 'verified' middleware and Registered-event auto-sending; arguably belongs with registration. No login/registration/notice/resend endpoints added.

issues.explanation: Three-field validation is done inline although conventions require a Form Request once rules grow beyond one or two fields.
Making User implement MustVerifyEmail is not required by the task and changes behaviour for the upcoming registration/login work (auto-sent verification, 'verified' middleware).
The guest-only test covers password.request and password.email but not password.reset/password.update.
Both views duplicate the head boilerplate including an unpinned CDN Bulma fallback without SRI.
Stray double blank line left in the template.

review.summary: The change delivers pt-BR, PegaFila-themed password-reset and verification e-mails, the guest password-reset flow with throttling and no address enumeration, and a signed/auth verification route, backed by thorough feature tests and updated docs/changelog. Remaining points are small: inline validation where a Form Request is the convention, an unrequested MustVerifyEmail on User, and minor view duplication, so it is approvable with nits.
